summary: Design how the sink emits fix tasks as real scheduled work (F781/#16 runtime wiring)

synthesis.winner: Design A — fix-round-as-second-scheduler-run (GOOSE_SWARM_FIX_SCHED), with one graft from Design B's verdict: shadow-aware judge probes for fix-mode tasks.
synthesis.rationale: A survived adversarial verification with ZERO fatal flaws and 8 small fixable issues; B has THREE fatal flaws (judge-abort vs shadow discipline, complete-fix:: prefix self-collision with its own race twins, drain-before-gate starvation by un-guarded idle-fill) whose mandatory repairs push it deeper into goose-swarm core (judge.rs exemptions, idle-fill suppression, exit-check rework) and change pause/exit semantics behind the lever. A touches ONLY crates/goose-cli/src/commands/swarm.rs, keeps the scheduler model-agnostic, keeps the measurement surface (pool_resolved.worker_count, fleet_models, fleet_slots, occupancy) untouched, and gets full scheduler machinery (claims, capacity, judge, tail-review) via a fresh Scheduler + fresh dispatcher — which structurally dodges the OnceLock, owner_snapshots, sink_review_findings, and device double-booking hazards that B must fight one by one. All non-negotiables hold in A: fix tasks are forced speculative via the proven fill:: mechanism, promotion is solely the unit-tested shard_beats_baseline strictly-< predicate, single-file rounds keep the race verbatim (branch untouched), and red-to-green-at-cap salvage survives because the shadow is graded even after fix_cap_secs timeout. HOWEVER, Verdict B exposed a flaw Verdict A missed that applies equally to A: the judge probe (swarm.rs ~20162-20201, verified at HEAD 0eea112a7) reads owned files, syntax, and the activity digest from CWD — the REAL tree — while fix agents write only their shadows, and speculative heartbeats land inside the shadow (13713-13716). Under default JudgeConfig this deterministically BrokenCode-kills every syntax-error fix at first inspection >=90s (the red file's syntax error is IN the real tree — that is why the fix task exists) and deterministic-Accepts/aborts compiling-tree fixes at ~420s ("not producing", stale mtime), gutting the fix run. The graft: a fix-mode-gated probe-root substitution (speculative_root when fix_round is Some and a shadow exists) — pure CLI-side, zero goose-swarm changes, run-1 behavior untouched. All 8 of Verdict A's fixable issues are folded into the commits below: judge/prereview env-gating mirrored, Dag::from_specs Err caught (never ? out of run_swarm), collision-proof #join id, notes_since_ms decided deliberately (run_started_ms — run-notes reach fix workers), max_attempts=1 for one-shot parity with today's fan (no retry-widened stale-baseline window, no attempts×cap wall-clock blowup), corrected join-delta facts in the load-bearing comment, clone-before-set for the owned contracts bundle, and by-value constructor args in the extraction. All anchor symbols re-verified at current HEAD 0eea112a7: fix_tasks_from_findings@22773, group_findings_by_file@22731, smoke_fix_description@22797, shard_beats_baseline@25399, spec_repair@25403, sink_shard@25275, fill:: branch@23231, run_with_decisions@2523, with_judge@2455, with_pre_reviewer@2464, with_sink@2488, with_pause_file@2496, with_doc_facts@2447, do_claim speculative:false@1053.
commits: COMMIT 1 (smallest, zero behavior change) — Lever: add fn fix_sched() -> bool resolver in crates/goose-cli/src/commands/swarm.rs following the sink_shard()@25275 / spec_repair()@25403 pattern: env GOOSE_SWARM_FIX_SCHED wins, else new `fix_sched: Option<bool>` config field, default OFF. Add "fix_sched" to the resolved-config event so campaign arms can attribute it. Unit test the resolver (env set / config set / neither). cargo fmt + clippy + test green; no call site reads it yet.

COMMIT 2 (pure refactor, byte-identical) — extract `async fn build_swarm_dispatcher(...) -> Result<Arc<GooseAgentDispatcher>>` from the constructor block at the GooseAgentDispatcher::new site (re-grep, ~26424-26450) and call it at the original site. Signature takes worker_extensions (Vec<ExtensionConfig>) and the resolver-derived args (stream_decode_retry_enabled etc., ~26442-26447) BY VALUE per call — call site clones — so a second dispatcher can be built later with identical semantics. Capture `let fix_devices: Vec<DeviceCfg> = devices.clone();` next to the existing fleet_models/fleet_slots/fleet_size captures (~28419-28423) BEFORE Scheduler::new moves devices at ~28424. Clone the contracts bundle / pillars / sink-tree values into locals BEFORE the set_contracts/set_pillars/sink-tree setter calls (verifier-corrected sites ~28208/28276/28284 — set_contracts takes ownership, comment at ~28148). cargo test green, no behavior change.

COMMIT 3 (dispatcher fix mode, dead code until commit 6) — add `fix_round: Mutex<Option<FixRound>>` {baseline: usize, lang: TargetLang, all_files: Vec<String>, round: usize} to GooseAgentDispatcher plus begin_fix_round()/end_fix_round() (end drains and discards leftover spec_shadows entries — bounds TempDir leak from judge-aborted tasks). In TaskDispatcher::run (@23218), next to the fill:: branch @23231-23258, add a `fix::` prefix branch gated on fix_round.is_some() (a coincidentally-named plan task can never trip it — mirror the fill_fan_enabled() gate comment): force req.speculative = true, substitute req.all_files from FixRound, wrap agent execution in tokio::time::timeout(fix_cap_secs()); install a Drop scopeguard IMMEDIATELY after make_shadow that removes the spec_shadows entry + drops the TempDir if the future is dropped before the epilogue disarms it (judge kills are JoinHandle aborts — no reachable-code audit can survive them; only Drop runs). Epilogue on every non-abort path: ALWAYS grade the shadow — run_smoke_gate(speculative_root(task_id), lang), g.ran==false => None — promote iff shard_beats_baseline(verified, baseline)@25399 else discard_speculative; a timed-out agent's partial shadow still competes (measured red-to-green-at-cap salvage). For the join task `fix::r{N}::#join` (owns all smoke files): re-gate the REAL tree first for the post_wave baseline and skip the agent entirely if that gate cannot run (mirror ~29342-29352). Fix mode no-ops generate_tests (kills the testgen seq-0 filename-collision hazard). Shadow-build failure stays a Transient bail (make_shadow insert overwrites @13405 so re-shadow is safe). Emit complete_fix_dispatched/complete_fix_completed with path:"sched". Load-bearing comment with CORRECTED facts: the fresh-dispatcher rule keeps owner_snapshots/OnceLock/sink_review_findings dead; the join deliberately keeps worker semantics — turn budget is PARITY with today's complete-fix::cross-file twin (max_turns keys on the literal id 'integrate-verify' @~24234); the genuinely new deltas are judge-killability and nonzero spiral budget; renaming it to integrate-verify would re-arm the fence-restore path. Unit tests: fix:: id with fix_round None passes through as ordinary task; promotion decisions (None never promotes, equal never promotes, strictly-less promotes, timed-out-but-strictly-better MUST promote); Drop guard discards shadow when future is dropped pre-epilogue.

COMMIT 4 (DAG builder) — add `fix_round_specs(findings, all_files, round, lang) -> Vec<TaskSpec>` beside fix_tasks_from_findings@22773: ids `fix::r{round}::{file}` from group_findings_by_file@22731's disjoint partition, deps: [] (roots, born Ready via dag.rs:106-110), descriptions via smoke_fix_description(&g.findings, lang)@22797 (lang threaded — no Python hardcode), owned_files: vec![file], Difficulty::Hard; when unassigned findings exist append `fix::r{round}::#join` — '#' cannot appear in a normalized file id, so a smoke file literally named 'join' can never collide — owning all smoke files with deps on every fix id. Unit tests extending the pattern @10701-10729: Dag::from_specs accepts the specs, roots are Ready, join is Pending until roots complete, and a file named 'join' does not collide with the join id.

COMMIT 5 (shadow-aware judge probe, CLI-side only, dead until commit 6) — in the Judge impl on GooseAgentDispatcher (probe region ~20162-20201: cwd resolution, owned-file metadata/mtime/read, syntax_error, and the .swarm/activity/<task_id>.json digest path), add `fn judge_probe_root(&self, task_id) -> PathBuf`: speculative_root(task_id) when fix_round.is_some() AND a spec_shadows entry exists, else cwd — and use it for BOTH the owned-file loop and the activity-digest path (speculative heartbeats live inside the shadow @13713-13716, so digest and files must come from the same root). Gating on fix_round keeps run-1 judge behavior (fill:: tasks, speculation twins) byte-identical. This makes the deterministic BrokenCode/Accept branches in goose-swarm's judge.rs operate on the tree the fix agent actually edits — without it, every syntax-error fix is BrokenCode-killed at ~90s (the syntax error is in the REAL tree by definition) and compiling trees are deterministic-Accept-aborted at ~420s (stale real-tree mtime + no digest = 'not producing'). Zero goose-swarm changes. Unit test the root selection (fix mode + shadow => shadow root; otherwise cwd).

COMMIT 6 (wire the second scheduler run behind the lever) — inside the shard arm (re-grep `else if (complete_parallel() || shard_this_round) && !fleet_models.is_empty()`, ~29206), when fix_sched(): build a FRESH dispatcher via build_swarm_dispatcher (same sink Arc => same JSONL; seed spec_frozen + set_contracts/set_pillars from the commit-2 cloned locals; pass run_started_ms — DELIBERATE: run-notes reach fix workers, re-delivery is context not a bug); begin_fix_round(verdict.findings.len() as the round-opening baseline, complete_lang, smoke_all_files, round); build `Scheduler::new(fix_devices.clone(), 1)` — max_attempts=1 for one-shot parity with today's fan: no retry-widened stale-baseline promotion window, no attempts x fix_cap_secs wall-clock blowup; a failed fix task costs nothing because the next round's gate regenerates fix tasks for still-red files — then .with_sink(sink).with_doc_facts(doc_facts).with_pause_file(same .swarm/pause), and wire .with_judge(fresh.clone(), judge_cfg) / .with_pre_reviewer(fresh.clone()) ONLY under the SAME env/config resolution as run 1 (mirror judge_on/prereview_on @~28442-28459 — an env-disabled judge must NOT reappear for fix rounds); NO replanner, NO speculation. Build the DAG with the Err CAUGHT: `match Dag::from_specs(fix_round_specs(...))` — on Err emit an event and continue the round loop exactly like the stuck-bail Err from run_with_decisions; never `?` out of run_swarm from the advisory fix path. Run run_with_decisions(dag, fresh as Arc<dyn TaskDispatcher>, fix_goal, user_decisions.clone()); on Err emit event + continue. Afterwards: end_fix_round(); drain the fresh dispatcher's sink_review_findings into an informational event; log the RunReport as complete_fix_sched_result WITHOUT feeding green_blocking_failed; check the complete cap_deadline immediately after the fix run returns (shared pause file means a desktop Pause can hold the run past complete_cap_secs — emit the overrun so the round-head cap logic fires next). The round loop's next real-tree run_smoke_gate stays the authoritative post-wave verify; GREEN/stall/cap/exit logic and the exit Err @~30213 untouched. Race arm (!shard_this_round) and serial 1-node path not modified. Lever OFF => byte-identical.

COMMIT 7 (regression tests + live verification + self-test) — tests: (a) lever-OFF leaves the shard arm unchanged (existing suite green); (b) a fix:: task never shadows when fix_round is unset; (c) salvage-parity promotion matrix (None/equal never, strictly-less always, timed-out-strictly-less promotes); (d) join-id collision test (file named 'join'); (e) Drop-guard closes the shadow on dropped future. Update goose-self-test.yaml, rebuild, run `goose run --recipe goose-self-test.yaml` per AGENTS.md. Then verify in the RUNNING app per campaign discipline (compiling is not evidence): one arm with GOOSE_SWARM_FIX_SCHED=1 on a multi-file red round; read complete_fix_completed path:"sched" events plus scheduler TaskDispatched/judge events for fix::r{N}:: ids; confirm judge events reference shadow state (no BrokenCode storm at ~90s on syntax-error fixes); confirm the real tree changed ONLY via spec_promote events on strictly-better counts; confirm lever-OFF arm output is unchanged.
open_risks: Judge kill still forfeits that attempt's red-to-green-at-cap salvage: abort lands at an await point before the grade epilogue and only the Drop guard runs (discard, never promote). Today's fan cannot abort before its cap, so this is a real per-attempt behavior delta — measure it (judge kill counts on fix:: ids) before any default-ON decision.

Deterministic Accept can still abort a FINISHED fix shadow in the small window between agent exit and grade completion (run_smoke_gate has await points) — wasteful, never unsafe (nothing promotes ungraded). Watch judge Accept events on fix:: ids in the measured arm; if frequent, a goose-swarm judge.rs by-name exemption (integrate-verify precedent @552/571) is the follow-up, breaking the zero-goose-swarm property.

Quality parity of scheduler-budgeted fix attempts (40-turn cap, spiral budget, repeat-break) vs today's wall-clock-only fan is unproven — LOWER CONFIDENCE here, on quality-parity not on safety; promote-only-strictly-better bounds the damage; campaign measurement is the deciding evidence.

Orphaned run-1 idle jobs (tail-review/pre-review spawned before the first scheduler returned) occupy LM Studio slots invisible to the fix scheduler's fresh in_flight=0 accounting — first-wave fix dispatches can stack on a busy node; bounded by those jobs' timeouts; degrades latency not correctness.
The fix run's tail-review findings drain to an informational event with no consumer; a later increment could feed them into the next round's findings.
fix_devices is cloned AFTER the planner push (~26374-26390), so a fix task can land on the planner model — inherited parity with today's fleet_models derivation, not new, but stated for the ledger.

swarm.rs is under active concurrent F781 commits (+24 line drift measured mid-analysis; today's session HEAD is 0eea112a7 but the round-loop and dispatcher regions are exactly where it edits) — every commit must re-grep the fn-name anchors (fix_tasks_from_findings, shard_beats_baseline, group_findings_by_file, the GooseAgentDispatcher::new block, the shard-arm condition) rather than trust line numbers; merge-conflict risk on the round-loop region is high.

Shared pause file: a desktop Pause during the fix run holds run_with_decisions open indefinitely and complete_cap_secs is only enforced at round heads — commit 6's post-run cap check emits the overrun but cannot preempt a paused run; documented behavioral delta behind the lever.

The fresh-dispatcher rule is load-bearing: anyone later reusing run-1's dispatcher for the fix run re-arms the OnceLock silent no-op, stale owner_snapshots restore, and sink_review_findings carryover; anyone renaming the join to 'integrate-verify' re-arms the fence-restore path. The commit-3 comment must survive refactors.

max_attempts=1 removes the Transient-retry path for shadow-build failures (make_shadow error => task fails, file waits for next round) — deliberate one-shot-parity trade; if measurement shows meaningful shadow-build flake, bump to 2 as its own attributable change.
synthesis.supervision_pool_answer: #14 — How hard is a second (supervision) device pool, and where does it plug in? MODERATE, not hard: ~5 scheduler predicates + 1 struct field + 1 CLI capture/thread + 1 event field, and NO dispatcher/consumer changes (every idle job reaches a device as a bare model_id string; LM Link routes by identifier; a dying supervision device wastes one idle job — timeouts yield JudgeOutcome::ok()/empty — and cannot fail the run; no prewarm needed since the pool source is resident `lms ps` models). Today there is exactly ONE pool: reconcile_pool_with_fleet (swarm.rs fn @2281, called @25984) builds one SwarmDevice per distinct LM Link identifier ('first host wins' dedup, so model_ids are unique fleet-wide by construction), servability-intersects @25993/26004, then GOOSE_SWARM_MAX_NODES (@26053-26097) sorts by configured speed_weight DESC and `capped.truncate(max)` @26083 drops the excluded tail ON THE FLOOR. That tail IS the natural supervision pool: `fleet_pool[max..]` captured before truncate — already servability-checked, resident, distinct model_ids. Plug points: (a) CLI @26077-26095 — capture the tail before truncate, convert via the same DeviceCfg mapping (@26353-26362, speed_weight_for), gate behind a default-OFF lever, and emit as a NEW pool_resolved field (\"supervision_devices\") WITHOUT touching worker_count @26408 — the field every harness reads as node-count ground truth; (b) swarm.rs @28424 — `.with_supervision_devices(sup_cfgs)` AFTER fleet_models/fleet_slots/fleet_size are captured (@28419-28423) so nothing derived from `devices` (spec-repair race width, fan-out permits, occupancy, smoke_fix_target, planner skeleton sizing) can drift; (c) scheduler.rs — add `supervision_only: bool` (default false) to DeviceCfg (@410-420) and APPEND flagged entries to the same State.devices vec (append-with-flag, NOT a second Vec: IdleSlotGuard.claimed_device @496 is a RAW INDEX with decrement @518-521, and appending keeps every build index valid). Then five predicate edits: pick_device filter @838 += !supervision_only (a build task on an excluded node is exactly the alphabetical-cap incident MAX_NODES exists to prevent); idle_capacity @736-742 counts build-only (else a '1-node' run trips the replan gate @2691 `>=2` and the idle-job last-slot-yield rule reads free slots that cannot build); least_loaded_free_device @1386-1393 ranks supervision first — key (!supervision_only, in_flight, i) — else an idle build node ties and WINS on index while the borrowed node sits free; pick_speculation_target excludes supervision (its twin is real build inference, or the 1-node arm label lies); stuck-bail @2662 reads a new build_in_flight() (sum over !supervision_only) so supervision idle jobs cannot mask a stuck DAG. Validation: the duplicate-model_id bail @2535-2538 must run over the UNION, and when the planner push (@26374-26390) collides with a supervision device's model_id, DROP the supervision entry (the model is already reachable) rather than bail. The genuinely delicate parts are measurement integrity (worker_count, fleet_models, fleet_slots, fleet_size, occupancy @30069-30087, and skeleton sizing must not move — keep the CLI `devices` vec untouched and hand the sup list over separately) and the three shared predicates (idle_capacity, total_in_flight, last-slot yield) whose consumers silently assume free slot == can build. Events need nothing: TaskDispatched/PreReview already carry device/model strings, and dispatched_per_device is only bumped by real dispatches (do_claim @984-991), so per-node build stats stay clean.

fixable_issues: Commit 5 wires judge + pre-reviewer unconditionally onto the fix scheduler; run 1 gates them on GOOSE_SWARM_JUDGE / GOOSE_SWARM_PREREVIEW (swarm.rs:28442-28459). As written, an env-disabled judge reappears for fix rounds — mirror the judge_on/prereview_on resolution when building the fix Scheduler.

Commit 5's `Dag::from_specs(fix_round_specs(...))?` propagates Err out of run_swarm, aborting the entire run from inside the advisory fix path. A smoke file literally named `join` produces id fix::r{N}::join colliding with the join task (from_specs bails on duplicate ids, dag.rs:97-98). Catch the Err like the stuck-bail Err (emit event, continue the round loop) and/or use a join id no file path can produce (e.g. fix::r{N}::#join — '#' can't appear in a normalized file id, same trick as the fill:: slot separator).

The notes_since_ms rationale is wrong as stated: a fresh dispatcher built via build_swarm_dispatcher with the same run_started_ms (constructor param 3, swarm.rs:13219/26428) has the identical notes epoch — freshness alone dodges nothing. Re-delivery of run-notes to fix agents is arguably desirable, but decide deliberately: pass run_started_ms (notes reach fix workers) or now_ms (only new notes do), and fix the design text.

Scheduler retries (Transient re-dispatch up to cfg.max_attempts, plus judge kill+re-dispatch) give a fix task multiple attempts where today's fan gives exactly one; each retry re-shadows from the CURRENT tree while the baseline stays round-opening, widening the stale-baseline promotion window (which already exists today when groups > fleet_slots, since promotion is inline per shard at 29311-29316), and widening worst-case round wall-clock to ~max_attempts x fix_cap_secs per task with the complete cap only checked at round heads (29033). Consider Scheduler::new(fix_devices, 1) for one-shot parity, or accept and measure — but state it; the design's risk list covers turn budgets, not attempt multiplicity.

Risk #7 overstates the join's regression: today's hand-built join twin (complete-fix::cross-file) already runs at the worker turn budget, because 24234 keys max_turns on the literal id 'integrate-verify'. The genuinely new join deltas are judge-killability and nonzero spiral budget only — the 120->40 turn claim is parity, not a loss. Correct the design text so the load-bearing fresh-dispatcher comment states the right facts.

Line-cite drift in the design: the contracts/pillars/sink-tree setters are called at 28208/28276/28284, not 28184/28252/28260, and set_contracts takes ownership of the bundle (comment at 28148) — commit 2's locals must be cloned BEFORE those set calls. spec_repair() is at 25403, group_findings_by_file at 22731. All consistent with the design's own re-grep-anchors rule; just re-anchor.

The shared pause file means a desktop Pause during the fix scheduler run holds run_with_decisions open indefinitely (all_terminal still exits, but non-terminal fix tasks hold), and the complete wall-clock cap is only checked at the next round head — today's fan is not pause-aware and always returns within ~fix_cap_secs per batch. Probably desired behavior, but it is a new way for the completion phase to exceed complete_cap_secs; note it or check cap_deadline after the fix run returns.

build_swarm_dispatcher must clone worker_extensions (Vec<ExtensionConfig>, moved into the constructor at 26430) and re-resolve or capture the resolver-derived constructor args (stream_decode_retry_enabled etc., 26442-26447) so the fix dispatcher matches run-1 semantics — straightforward, but the commit-2 extraction signature must take them by value per call, not move-once.
verdicts.verdict: FEASIBLE — the design survives adversarial verification against HEAD (0eea112a7, still current). Every load-bearing structural claim checks out in the actual code: run_with_decisions is &self with fully per-call State (scheduler.rs:2523-2605) so a second run on a fresh Scheduler is clean; all assumed builders exist with the assumed signatures (with_sink 2488, with_doc_facts 2447, with_pause_file 2496, with_judge+JudgeConfig::default 2455/28448, with_pre_reviewer 2464); the fill:: forced-speculative precedent is exactly as cited (23231-23258) and the fix:: branch slots in before the shadow decision at 23267; shard_beats_baseline is at 25399 verbatim (strictly <, None never promotes); the shard arm, baseline (verdict.findings.len(), 29216), inline per-shard promotion (29311-29316), and the join's post-wave re-gate with skip (29348-29352) all match the parity claims; Dag::from_specs births indegree-0 roots Ready (dag.rs:106-110); the exit gate at 30214 is untouched by the advisory fix report. The two candidate fatal flaws I hunted hardest both dissolve on inspection: (1) no double promote/discard — the scheduler contains ZERO calls to promote_speculative/discard_speculative (they are default-no-op trait methods only the CLI fan calls today), so dispatcher-internal promotion is sole owner of the lifecycle; (2) no torn promote under judge kill — kills are AbortHandle::abort() which only lands at await points, and promote_speculative's body (24544-24566) is await-free synchronous fs code, so a kill forfeits salvage (the design's stated risk) but cannot half-copy the real tree. The fresh-dispatcher answers to the OnceLock (14789-14801 silent no-op), owner_snapshots (23282/24451 — capture gated on !speculative), and sink_review_findings hazards are correct, and the constructor (13216-13274) is cheap enough to rebuild per round. Shadow discipline and the verdict chain are genuinely preserved: fix tasks cannot write the real tree except via the same unit-tested strictly-better predicate, and final_passed still comes only from the round loop's real-tree gate. Eight fixable issues found (judge/prereview env opt-outs ignored, from_specs `?` aborting the run on a constructible join-id collision, the false notes_since_ms rationale, retry-widened stale-baseline/wall-clock windows, an overstated join turn-budget delta, setter line-cite drift with a clone-before-set requirement, pause-past-cap, and constructor-arg cloning) — all are small, none undermines the architecture. Where my confidence is lower, per the design's own framing: quality-parity of scheduler-budgeted fix attempts vs today's wall-clock-only fan is unproven and correctly deferred to campaign measurement; feasibility and safety are high-confidence.

fatal_flaws: JUDGE ABORT vs SHADOW DISCIPLINE (default-ON path): the scheduler judge kills via JoinHandle abort (scheduler.rs 1842-1843 Accept, 1963-1964 terminal, 2066-2067 re-dispatch; handles registered at 2648-2654) — cancellation at an await point runs NO epilogue code, so Commit 4's 'audit every early-return/DispatchError path so a judge kill can never skip the grade+close epilogue' is structurally impossible as stated. Worse, every judge probe reads the REAL tree while a forced-speculative fix agent writes only its shadow: owned files, syntax check, and the activity digest are all resolved against cwd (swarm.rs 20162-20201), and speculative heartbeats deliberately stay inside the shadow (13713-13716). Consequences for a spliced complete-fix task under the DEFAULT config (judge ON, swarm.rs 28442-28448): (a) if the finding is a syntax error in the owned file — the commonest smoke redness — deterministic BrokenCode (judge.rs 365-378, no elapsed floor) fires at the first inspection ≥90s, the agent is aborted and re-queued, twice, then terminal-failed at the intervention cap: the fix never gets its 1200s budget; (b) if the file compiles, deterministic Accept (judge.rs 543-568: all owned present with old real-tree content, compile clean, mtime already ≥420s stale from the build phase, no digest → not producing) fires at the first inspection past 420s elapsed — the agent is aborted, the task marked Done, NOTHING is promoted, and the spec_shadows entry + TempDir leak for the rest of the process. Any fix running past ~7 minutes is silently discarded and the next gate invocation sees an unchanged tree, burning the round budget. This inverts the design's claimed benefit 'judge supervision applies for free'. Repair is bounded but mandatory: exempt complete-fix:: ids from pick_judge_target / the deterministic branches (crib integrate-verify's by-name exemptions, judge.rs 552/571) and close shadows via a Drop guard, not a path audit.

PREFIX SELF-COLLISION: Commit 2's dispatcher branch `task_id.starts_with("complete-fix::")` intercepts the design's OWN retained in-callback race twins — the Repaired path runs the race body verbatim, which dispatches ids `complete-fix::twin{i}` through the very same TaskDispatcher::run (swarm.rs 29081, me.run at 29123). run_gate_fix would then grade and promote EACH twin independently against gate_round_baseline (twins own ALL app files, so multiple whole-tree promotes clobber each other — exactly what pick_repair_winner's single-winner rule exists to prevent, 25409+), after which the race body performs its own promote/discard per twin (29183-29190), double-closing already-removed spec_shadows entries and violating the exactly-one-close contract (13421-13435). The risks section only considers foreign planner ids; the design's own path trips it. Must match the spliced shape exactly (e.g. strip_prefix("complete-fix::r") + digit + "::"), which is safe since the shard fan (whose ids are complete-fix::<file>) is replaced by the spliced path when the lever is ON.

DRAIN-BEFORE-GATE SELF-STARVATION: the design waits for total_in_flight()==0 before the first gate invocation, but the exit check (2657) precedes the idle-fill blocks (2836-3021), which run every pass with NO all_terminal guard and explicitly 'saturate ALL free nodes' via inner loops (2893, 2928). Tail-review is default ON (scheduler.rs 62-71) with a per-run cap of 40, pre-review is default ON (swarm.rs 28454-28459) and targets every Done owns-files task not yet reviewed. So after the last task completes, each loop pass REFILLS the slots the drain is waiting to empty: in_flight==0 is unreachable until the tail-review budget and pre-review targets exhaust — potentially 25-40 reviews × ~90s+ before the FIRST gate invocation, repeated with remaining budget between fix generations. The design suppresses only pick_testgen and only after invocation 1. Idle-fill must be suppressed whenever all_terminal && gate-unsettled; without it the lever's headline benefit (fix rounds inside the run) is eaten by review churn and the design's own 'hung idle job deadlocks the exit' risk is realized through continuous respawning, not orphans.
fixable_issues: GateRoundState 'drift (computed ONCE, as pre-loop today at 28698)' cannot be computed at set_gate_state time: the setter runs at the 28516 wiring region BEFORE run_with_decisions, and cross_module_drift reads the DELIVERED tree (28698-28709 runs post-scheduler today). Computed pre-run it is vacuous/wrong. Must be lazily computed inside the first evaluate() (arm is default OFF, so severity is low, but the stated design is incorrect).

gate_invocations accounting is self-contradictory in Commit 1: the apply list increments the counter only on Repaired, while FixTasks does 'splice + continue' — so an always-FixTasks gate never trips GATE_MAX_INVOCATIONS (bounded only by the CLI rounds counter) and the pick_testgen guard (gate_invocations>0) never arms; yet the test list claims 'always-Fix hits the invocation cap'. Increment on every non-settling outcome.

The testgen-poisoning guard misses the invocation-0 window: during the drain wait before the FIRST invocation gate_invocations==0, so pick_testgen (when the arm is ON) can still spawn and write real-tree test files into the tree the opening baseline will grade. Guard should key on gate-present && all_terminal, not on invocations.

fix_tasks_from_findings hardcodes TargetLang::Python in smoke_fix_description (swarm.rs 22782-22783) — the Commit 2 signature change must also thread complete_lang or non-Python runs get Python fix/verify instructions in every spliced task description.

The post-return 'ONE authoritative final verify' must re-run the FULL conjunct set (missing_source_deliverables re-stat, drift re-append, http_timeout_scan, spec_contract), not just run_smoke_gate — today final_passed/complete_failed derive from the union of all conjunct findings (28739-28932, 28935-28986), and a smoke-only final verify can flip a verdict the gate reached on a non-smoke conjunct.

Even with a judge exemption, close the shadow with a Drop/scopeguard inside run_gate_fix rather than relying on reachable code paths: dispatcher-internal kills (omni-judge, repeat-breaker) are auditable early returns, but the scheduler retains other abort sources (apply_split at 2204, speculation at 1193) and any future one silently reintroduces the leak; the design's own gate_spliced speculation guard is correct and necessary (pick_speculation_target reuses the primary task_id, 1652-1706, and a twin's make_shadow would drop the primary's TempDir mid-flight, 13405-13419).

Minor wording landmine: 'Single-group/1-model rounds keep the existing spec-repair race verbatim' — with fleet_models.len()==1 the copied body's race condition (29053) is false and execution falls to the SERIAL path (29418+, speculative:false, direct real-tree write) in-callback. That matches today's deliberate 1-node behavior and is safe only because the loop is blocked at in_flight==0, but the 'preserves' claim that the serial real-tree path is unreachable must be scoped to scheduler-dispatched tasks, and a test should pin that multi-model fleets can never route serial in-callback.
verdicts.verdict: Feasible with mandatory corrections — the architecture verifies against the code, but three of its claims are false as written. Verified sound at HEAD 0eea112a7 (design line refs still exact): the CompletionGate trait mirror of Replanner (replan.rs 28-33, with_replanner 2503), gate state on the per-call State, the unconditional all_terminal return at 2657-2661 being the correct interception point, splice_specs semantics (dag.rs 197-313: validate-then-commit, deps=[] born Ready, caller pushes the heap), bonus exclusion from green_blocking_failed, fix_tasks_from_findings's TaskSpec shape, do_claim's hardcoded speculative:false (1053) overridden dispatcher-side exactly as the fill:: precedent does (23231-23258), make_shadow insert-overwrite retry safety, exactly-one-close promote/discard (24544-24572), shard_beats_baseline strictly-< (25399), per-task promotion matching today's shard-fan discipline (29311-29316), and — critically — the replanner call is an INLINE await in the loop (2711-2719), so the whole scheduler (including all idle-fill) is blocked during evaluate(), which is what actually makes the in-callback race's private fanout semaphore safe, over and above the in_flight==0 precondition. The refutation stands on three points: (1) the default-ON judge kills by JoinHandle ABORT and probes only the REAL tree (files, syntax, activity all at cwd, swarm.rs 20162-20201) while fix agents work in shadows — syntax-error findings get the fix task BrokenCode-killed at ~90s and terminal-failed before its budget, compiling trees get deterministic-Accept-aborted at 420s with the fix silently discarded; Commit 4's path audit cannot survive an abort, so complete-fix:: must be judge-exempted (integrate-verify precedent, judge.rs 552/571) and shadow closure moved to a Drop guard — 'judge supervision applies for free' is inverted, not free; (2) the starts_with(\"complete-fix::\") dispatcher branch hijacks the design's own retained race twins (complete-fix::twin{i} through the same run(), 29081/29123), causing multi-promote of whole-tree shadows plus double-close — the match must be narrowed to the r{n}:: shape; (3) waiting for total_in_flight()==0 while the loop's un-guarded idle-fill blocks keep saturating every free node (2893/2928; tail-review default ON, cap 40) starves the first gate invocation for up to the remaining review budget — idle-fill must be suppressed under all_terminal+gate-unsettled. Plus one state-timing error: drift cannot live in a pre-run GateRoundState since it reads the delivered tree (28698). All four repairs are local and stay within the proposed architecture; nothing found requires a redesign. Remaining stated risks (concurrent F781 edits to the same regions, copied-not-moved round body divergence, deferred join twin costing a round) are real and correctly characterized by the design.
